newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Salem 2 nuke repairs seen lasting all weekend.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Salem 2 nuke repairs seen lasting all weekend.

text.p: Public Service Electric & Gas Co (PSE&G) said Friday repair work on the 1,106 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Salem nuclear power plant in southern New Jersey will likely continue through the weekend.
After discovering problems with the unit's spray valves midweek, engineers cooled the reactor to "hot shutdown" from "hot standby" status.
"We have to complete repairs on these valves. We have to retest that it (the unit) will operate properly," said a PSE&G spokeswoman.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) earlier today said it was waiting to hear from PSE&G whether it completed the repairs before it would grant restart approval for Salem 2.
PSE&G hoped to startup Salem 2 before the end of July.
Salem 2 and adjoining unit 1 with the same generating capacity have been shut for more than two years due to safety concerns raised by the NRC.
Salem 2 was physically ready to resume operation before the valve problem cropped up.
In addition to PSE&G, PECO Energy Co, Atlantic Energy Co and Delmarva Power & Light Co are part-owners of the Salem units.
